content: Acrivastine is a pharmaceutical agent utilized in the management of allergic conditions, including hay fever. It functions as a second-generation H1-receptor antagonist antihistamine, similar to its parent compound, triprolidine. Its mechanism of action involves the inhibition of histamine H1 receptors, thereby mitigating allergic symptoms. Unlike first-generation antihistamines, acrivastine is classified as a non-sedating antihistamine, meaning it is less likely to cause drowsiness. In the United Kingdom, acrivastine is marketed under the brand name Benadryl Allergy Relief by McNeil Laboratories. It is important to note that this product is distinct from Benadryl Once a Day, which contains cetirizine, another antihistamine also sold by McNeil in the UK. Additionally, acrivastine serves as the active ingredient in the Semprex brand. A related product, Semprex-D, combines acrivastine with the decongestant pseudoephedrine and is manufactured by Actient Pharmaceuticals. When compared to other widely used antihistamines such as cetirizine or loratadine, which are typically administered as a single daily dose, acrivastine may be taken up to three times per day. However, it is contraindicated in certain populations, including individuals over the age of 65, pregnant women, and those with impaired liver or kidney function.
